Subject: Regional handoff priority & RPO exception request — FinVault

Diego,

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. As we start planning our go-live next quarter, a couple of DR questions came up from our platform team that are blocking procurement:

- We need an explicit regional handoff priority defined for multi-region failover (us-east primary, eu-west preferred fallback) so that our compliance team can sign off.
- FinVault requires a 1-hour RTO and 30-minute RPO for a subset of payments traffic (payments-processor service).

We understand those are tighter than your baseline. Can Redwood provide an SLA carveout or exception for the payments-processor workload (estimated 120 qps) and outline the operational changes, pricing delta, and liability cap?

I've attached our DR requirements spreadsheet for reference (finvault-dr-requirements.xlsx). Please loop in whoever needs to evaluate feasibility and cost.

Best,
Julia Smith
Director, Platform Engineering
FinVault

Diego / team — quick technical assessment below. Quoted the customer's asks for clarity.

> they want a prioritized failover (us-east -> eu-west) and a 1h RTO / 30m RPO for payments (~120 qps).

Reality check: baseline Hosted/Dedicated patterns give us ~RTO 1–3 hours depending on warm resources; RPO is usually several minutes to hours depending on replication mode. For 30m RPO at 120 qps for payments, options:

1) Active-passive warm-standby (replicated state + pre-warmed compute in eu-west): achievable RTO ~45–90m, RPO near 1–30m if we enable near-real-time streaming replication; requires reserved capacity in eu-west and write-forward replication to a geo-replica.

2) Active-active across regions with cross-region replication: RTO ~ <30m but increases complexity (consistency, conflict resolution) and substantial ongoing cost. Not typically available as standard offering.

Engineering constraints / costs:
- To guarantee 30m RPO we must enable WAL/streaming replication and increase persistence frequency; this increases egress and storage overhead.
- We should carve the payments-processor service out as a named workload and enforce routing to a dedicated pool with pinned KV caches to avoid cold-warm overhead on failover.
- We'll need a runbook for manual switchover with an automated canary (traffic shift in 10% increments) and a rollback path.

Recommendation: offer a "Warm-Standby Premium" SOW: target RTO = 60m (contracted), best-effort 45m operational target; RPO = 30m guaranteed with technical controls. Require reserved capacity in eu-west and a 12-month commit. Add explicit SLA credit schedule and a liability cap for the carveout.

I'll draft the technical appendix and required infra delta today.

— Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Regional handoff priority & RPO exception request — FinVault

Diego / team,

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with my thinking. Commercially, we should treat this as a premium add-on ("Warm-Standby Premium"). Proposed commercial outline: 

- 12-month reserved commitment for the payments-processor pool (min capacity: 2x steady-state to cover failover).
- Monthly uplift: +40% on top of standard Dedicated pricing for that pool to cover reserved standby, replication egress, and on-call ops.
- One-time setup fee to cover runbook and DR tests: $25k.
- SLA: Contracted RTO = 60 minutes, RPO = 30 minutes. SLA credits schedule to be drafted; liability for this carveout limited to 3 months of net service fees for the carved workload (we can discuss cap).

Lauren — can legal draft a short addendum that: (a) names the payments-processor workload, (b) maps the failover order (us-east primary, eu-west fallback), and (c) accepts our proposed liability cap?

If we can agree to those bullets, I'll draft the external reply and attach the pricing sheet + SOW.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: standby-pricing-sheet.pdf

Julia — thanks for the patience while we scoped this with engineering and commercial. Below is our proposed approach for the payments-processor workload and the next steps if you want to proceed.

Proposed term summary (Warm-Standby Premium):
- Named workload: payments-processor (FinVault) — traffic ~120 qps
- Regional failover priority: us-east (primary) -> eu-west (preferred fallback)
- Contracted SLA: RTO = 60 minutes (operational target 45 minutes), RPO = 30 minutes (guaranteed)
- Operational requirements: 12-month reserved capacity in eu-west, pinned compute pool + WAL streaming replication enabled, quarterly DR runbooks and one annual full failover test (remote witness)
- Pricing: Reserved uplift +40% on Dedicated for the named pool; $25k one-time setup fee (runbook + DR test)
- Liability cap for this carveout: equal to 3 months of net service fees for the named workload (subject to legal review)

Next steps:
1) If you accept the above, we'll issue a Warm-Standby SOW and a short SLA addendum. Link to draft SOW: https://redwood.app/sow/FV-STD-2027-v1 (internal preview).
2) Sign via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/XYZ-123-FV.
3) Deliverables after signing: infra reservation in eu-west scheduled within 10 business days, runbook handoff, and a DR test window within 30–45 days.

Lauren / Grace — please confirm legal language and attach the SOW + pricing doc to the envelope when ready.

Julia — happy to hop on a quick 30m call tomorrow to walk the terms if helpful.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-standby-sow-v1.docx
